mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing government authority of the UBO's jurisdiction, attested by a recognized notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the designated Competent Authority in the country of document origin; for non-Hague Convention states, consular legalization by the issuing country's consulate and the Legalization Section of Global Affairs Canada

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, tax authority, or bank of the beneficial owner's residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, together with certified English or French translation where the source document is not in English or French

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Status / Certificate of Good Standing of any foreign corporate shareholder or intermediate holding company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or competent corporate registrar of the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders holding 25% or more of voting shares or control rights, family-office principals, and any nominees or intermediaries against: (i) FINTRAC politically exposed persons (PEP) indicators; (ii) Canadian regulations implementing United Nations Security Council sanctions and asset freezes; (iii) the Special Economic Measures Act target list; (iv) the Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act list; (v) the United States OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List where USD wire activity is contemplated; and (vi) consolidated global assurance lists. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for this Medium_Risk_Enhanced single-family-office structure, requiring senior-management approval, written risk rating, and ongoing transaction monitoring where a PEP or proximity to a PEP is identified.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Corporate Registry - Corporate Online (British Columbia Registries, https://www.bcregistry.gov.bc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A BC business corporation name must consist of a distinctive element, a descriptive element where required by the Registrar, and a permissible legal element such as 'Company', 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Limited', or an abbreviation. Names in a non-Latin script must be transliterated into Roman characters in an approved form; English and French accents are permitted. The Registrar applies similarity and misleading-connotation tests against existing BC corporate names, extraprovincial registered names, and protected marks.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registrar refuses a proposed name, the applicant may: (1) file a new or amended name reservation through BC Corporate Online with written written submissions addressing the refusal grounds and attaching any required consent letters; (2) request reconsideration by the Registrar of Companies within 21 days of the refusal; and (3) if reconsideration is unsuccessful, petition the Supreme Court of British Columbia for judicial review under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 241. Name reservations are not extendable; if incorporation is not completed within 56 days, a new name reservation application and fee are required.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted with conditions for a single-family-office holding entity. The registered office and records office must be a physical address in British Columbia at which service of process can be made and corporate records are maintained. A serviced-office or registered-agent address satisfies the statutory requirement, but a post-office box alone is insufficient. The absence of a dedicated physical office is generally acceptable where the company does not engage in regulated trust, lending, or investment-dealing activity requiring physical premises.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; estimated probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months of normal operation is below 10%. The likelihood increases materially if the company exhibits FINTRAC/CRA risk indicators, such as abrupt changes in ownership, inconsistent source-of-funds documentation, nominee arrangements, or repeated third-party fund movements.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57, ss. 3-12 (incorporation), ss. 194-196 (registered office and records office), ss. 173-179 (directors and officers), and Part 10 (share capital)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registrar of Companies, British Columbia Corporate Registry, Service BC
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application and Notice of Articles filed through BC Corporate Online
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; shares may be issued without par value and need not be fully paid at incorporation; no escrow or capital deposit account is required under the BC Business Corporations Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: 1. The incorporation application, Notice of Articles and Articles filed with the British Columbia Registrar of Companies are approved and adopted. 2. The registered office and records office of the Company shall be at [address], British Columbia, as set out in the Notice of Articles, until changed by the directors. 3. The share subscriptions set out in the subscription schedule are approved; the directors are authorised to issue certificates for those shares. 4. [Name] is appointed President and [Name] is appointed Secretary, each to hold office until removed by the Board. FURTHER RESOLVED that officers are authorised to execute documents and open bank accounts necessary for the Company's single-family office purposes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry, Corporate Online portal (Service BC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the BC corporate name database to ensure the proposed name is distinguishable and not prohibited. Submit a name reservation request via BC Corporate Online with up to three alternative names. The name reservation is valid for 56 days. No notarization is required.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and two alternative names
Specified choice of corporate designation (Inc., Corp., Ltd., or Ltd.)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as confusing or non-distinctive, file a revised name reservation request with a new proposed name or provide a consent from an existing holder to use a confusingly similar name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Incorporation Documents and Director Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Incorporation Application (Form 1), Notice of Articles (Form 2), Articles, and consents from the first directors. Have the incorporators and first directors sign the application and articles. Verify the registered office address is a physical address in British Columbia and select a records office address, which may be the registered office address.
required_dossiers: Signed consent of each first director to act as director
Registered office and records office address details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry queries missing signatures or incomplete information, correct the affected form and resubmit through BC Corporate Online within the cure period indicated in the registry notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing and Payment of Incorporation Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to BC Corporate Online and complete the incorporation transaction by entering the company's name, share structure, directors, and registered office information. Upload or transcribe the prepared Form 1, Form 2, and Articles as required by the online system. Pay the applicable incorporation fee of CAD 350 by accepted payment method and retain the transaction receipt.
required_dossiers: Articles and Notice of Articles in accepted electronic format
Payment confirmation for the filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the payment fails or the filing is rejected due to incorrect data, contact the BC Registry Support Desk or resubmit the corrected application electronically; any paid fee will be applied to the successful filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful filing, the Certificate of Incorporation is issued by the Registrar. Verify the company summary, the Certificate of Incorporation, Notice of Articles, and initial share allotment. Record the certificate and registered documents in the Company's corporate records book, and issue share certificates for the subscribed shares.
required_dossiers: Filed Notice of Articles and Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate or Notice of Articles contains typographical or registry errors, request a correction through the BC Corporate Registry and provide supporting evidence of the correct particulars.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Provincial Tax Registration and Business Number Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and BC Provincial Tax Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the CRA for a federal Business Number and the corporate income tax account (program account RC0001). Register for GST/HST if threshold requirements are met. Register with the BC Revenue Services for provincial corporate tax and any applicable provincial programs. Open the company's corporate bank account and provide a copy of the Certificate of Incorporation and Notice of Articles to the bank.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening form and initial resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA or provincial registry rejects the tax registration due to name or address mismatch, verify and correct the corporate records with BC Registry, then resubmit the CRA application online or by paper as instructed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial licensing board is engaged for a pure investment holding single-family office under NAICS 525920 and ISIC 6430.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None — no operating or manufacturing permit is required for the single-family office's passive investment holding business model.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no EIA registration or full assessment is required in the absence of physical industrial operations or construction.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — the single-family office does not own or operate a facility subject to BC Environmental Management Act permitting, wastewater discharge authorizations, VOC emission controls, or hazardous waste registration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Occupancy permit issued by the local municipality under the BC Building Code and fire safety verification by the local fire authority; WorkSafeBC registration and occupational health and safety compliance apply to office operations. No additional industrial structural clearance is required for a non-manufacturing investment office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada; official portal: https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html, including Business Registration Online and My Business Account. For British Columbia: the BC Ministry of Finance administers the Provincial Sales Tax and Employer Health Tax; BC Corporate Registry administers corporate statute filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Canadian business corporation: (1) incorporate under the Canada Business Corporations Act or the BC Business Corporations Act, and if federally incorporated then register extraprovincially in British Columbia; (2) obtain the 9-digit CRA Business Number (BN) through CRA Business Registration Online or Form RC1; (3) activate the GST/HST account, payroll deductions account, and corporate income tax account as applicable; (4) if carrying on a taxable activity in BC, register with BC Corporate Registry and, where required, for BC PST and Employer Health Tax; (5) maintain a Canadian registered office, records of directors, an authorized representative, and a current CRA correspondence address.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: A Canadian business corporation is a separate taxable legal person under Part I of the Income Tax Act, taxed on worldwide income if resident in Canada and on Canadian-source income if non-resident. The entity is not pass-through and no US-style check-the-box election exists. British Columbia imposes provincial corporate income tax on income allocated to the province.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a check-the-box election or a hybrid mismatch election; entity classification is statutory under the Income Tax Act and Excise Tax Act. Relevant elections and designations include: (i) the GST/HST related-corporation joint election under ETA section 156 to treat supplies between closely related registrants as not a taxable supply; (ii) the non-resident corporation election under ITA section 216 for net-basis taxation of Canadian rental or timber income; (iii) capital dividend account and eligible dividend designations for Canadian-controlled private corporations; (iv) associated-corporation designations affecting the small business deduction. Anti-hybrid and foreign affiliate dumping rules apply automatically without elective relief.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) federal value-added tax, with British Columbia imposing a separate 7% Provincial Sales Tax under the Provincial Sales Tax Act.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000: a person making taxable supplies in Canada becomes a mandatory GST/HST registrant once total worldwide taxable supplies in any preceding four consecutive calendar quarters exceed C$30,000. BC PST registration is separately required for vendors selling taxable goods, software, or services in BC, without a comparable minimum threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No national real-time fiscal clearance, API pre-authorization, or digital stamping regime exists for invoices in Canada. CRA accepts electronic invoices and records; registrants must preserve prescribed invoice and record data in a readable format and e-file GST/HST returns when required. Export declarations must be submitted electronically through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) to the Canada Border Services Agency.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A registered person may zero-rate (0% GST/HST) supplies of tangible personal property exported from Canada, as well as services and intangible property supplied to a non-resident where the supply is not for consumption or use in Canada and is not related to Canadian real property or Canadian goods. Financial services, including many investment and family-office management services, are generally exempt rather than zero-rated and must be characterized with care. The exporter must retain evidence that the recipient is non-resident and, for services, that the benefit is not realized in Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Export Declaration transmitted through CERS (Canadian Export Reporting System), including any required export permits
Commercial invoice describing the goods or services, quantity, value, and contracting parties
Bill of Lading, Airway Bill, or other transport document proving physical export from Canada
Inward Remittance Certificate, bank SWIFT MT103 credit advice, or equivalent financial evidence of receipt of the export consideration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may deny zero-rating, reassess within the normal four-year period, extended to ten years in cases of misrepresentation, fraud, or neglect, recover uncollected GST/HST plus statutory interest, and impose civil penalties for false statements or gross negligence. Criminal tax evasion or materially false export claims attract fines and imprisonment under the Excise Tax Act, Income Tax Act, and Criminal Code.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) combined with the federal prudential supervisor, the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI). Canada maintains no central-bank foreign exchange control department; currency policy is free-market oriented and the Bank of Canada does not license or approve individual cross-border treasury transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains de jure and de facto full convertibility of the Canadian dollar on both current and capital account. The Currency Act, the Bank of Canada Act, and customary international law impose no exchange-rate approval, surrender, or repatriation licensing for family office capital. Profit remittance from a British Columbia business corporation is achieved via board-declared dividends; the only meaningful friction is Canadian withholding tax under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (normally 25% absent a treaty, subject to reduced rates under the Canada-US treaty or other applicable tax treaties) and the obligation to remit withholding promptly to the Canada Revenue Agency. FINTRAC cross-border reporting thresholds apply to cash and international electronic funds transfers, but these are reporting obligations, not convertibility restrictions. No hurdles exist under the provincial British Columbia Business Corporations Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender period, mandatory conversion ratio, or repatriation deadline for Canadian export proceeds. Export receipts may be retained indefinitely in foreign currency. For regulatory completeness, incoming export payments of CAD 10,000 or more must be discloseable to FINTRAC as international electronic funds transfers by the Canadian financial institution, and customs export documentation must match Canadian trade declarations; however, no proceeds surrender to the Bank of Canada or any regulatory authority is required. Commercial banking counterparties generally require standard supporting invoices and bills of lading for trade settlement but do not impose currency conversion surrenders.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Montreal (BMO Bank of Montreal)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with integrated Global Transaction Banking
Operational Account / Private Wealth Treasury Account
Operational Account / Escrow Account for Investment Vehicles

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating for a BC single-family office using offshore digital EMIs as a primary treasury rail is Low. Canadian banking law requires a corporation conducting core banking relationships through a regulated Canadian bank or an authorized foreign bank branch under the Bank Act (Canada) and OSFI licensing. Pure EMIs are not members of Payments Canada and cannot offer CDIC-insured deposits. An offshore EMI may be used only as a supplementary, low-value disbursement channel if it is registered as a money services business (MSB) in Canada with FINTRAC, maintains adequate sanctions screening, and avoids the phrase 'bank account' in favor of 'e-money account.' For capital escrow, custody, and cross-currency clearing, a Schedule I Canadian bank or licensed Schedule II authorized foreign bank branch remains mandatory. Feasibility rating: Medium for ancillary operating expenses and small disbursements; Low for primary treasury concentration.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian AML law does not statutorily mandate physical presence of every director for corporate account opening. Remote onboarding is permitted if the bank can satisfy client identification requirements under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, including digital liveness verification, notarized certified corporate documents, and identity evidence of signatories. In practice, for a single-family office with foreign beneficial owners and anticipated cross-border wire activity, Canadian banks commonly impose an in-person interview with the principal beneficial owner or a board-appointed treasury officer at the branch, private banking center, or foreign representative office to verify source of wealth. The standard is Moderate to High physical expectation: schedule videoconference first, but be prepared for one physical registry/attorney supported appearance, particularly for signatory authority over capital escrow accounts. Required bundle must include certified copies of the federal/provincial incorporation documents, the BC extraprovincial registration if applicable, register of directors, ultimate beneficial ownership declaration, and legal opinions for trust or estate sources of wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner classified as or associated with a politically exposed person (PEP) in any jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source of wealth report covering 24 months of independent bank and custody statements; provenance of initial capital from legal establishment of the family office; certified tax returns from residence jurisdiction(s); employment or business-sale contracts; official PEP-assessment questionnaire; an explanation of legitimate government-networked business history; and a written private-wealth professional opinion confirming the absence of unexplained wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Thin capitalization or inconsistent operating purpose of the single-family office investment holding company.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved business plan and investment mandate showing family-asset management, not unilateral trade finance; consolidated portfolio list with ISINs and custody evidence; audited or accountant-reviewed financial statements; the intercompany or investment advisory agreement; source of funds traces from grantor/settlor accounts; proof of registered office and substance in British Columbia; and transaction-flow predictions covering projected valuations, lending, and shareholder distributions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdictions linked to settlor, trust situs, or underlying portfolio counterparties, including sanctions-listed or FATF-monitored states.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed economic purpose memorandum explaining the family office's presence in Canada; clean global sanctions and EFTA/FATF screening certificates; legal opinions from the jurisdiction of the trust and the jurisdiction of the settlor; assignment of equitable title documentation for trust assets; and confirmation from professional intermediaries that the business activities do not touch prohibited sectors such as nuclear proliferation, arms, or sanctioned commodity trade.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from an offshore trust or foreign limited partnership without a visible nexus to Canadian operations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Final or certified trust deed and schedule of beneficiaries; trust protector approval; chain-of-funds ledger from the initial gift or family business sale to the Canadian investment holding account; share certificates issued in exchange for the contribution; a board resolution for issuance at par or stated capital; register of share transfers; tax-domicile certificates; and a response memorandum demonstrating that no unreported foreign source income is being laundered through the BC corporation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency cross-border wires or structured transfers inconsistent with the family office investment mandate, triggering FINTRAC large value and management-flagged reporting.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A treasury and investment policy statement approved by the board, limiting counterparties and instruments to low-leverage private/public equities, fixed income, and permitted hedging; monthly reconciliation of SWIFT messages to custodian confirms and trade tickets; an organizational chart separating the treasury officer from beneficial ownership; an external audit trail of the clearing route; and escalation protocols to ensure all MT103/MF202 transfers are documented with written investment or flow-of-funds contracts.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a compliant inbound capital injection into the British Columbia single-family office, the preferred rail is SWIFT MT103 from the settlor/beneficial owner's high-street bank to the Canadian bank account using the corporate SWIFT BIC, Canadian bank transit number and account number. Payment messages should state 'Issued Share Capital Contribution' or 'Equity Subscription' in SWIFT field 70 where permitted, accompanied by the board authorization and share allotment. The corresponding SWIFT purpose tag should align with Canadian balance-of-payments accounting as a direct investment equity transaction rather than trade-in-goods. The Canadian receiving bank applies OSFI-mandated sanctions screening and FINTRAC reporting when the transaction is CAD 10,000 or greater. Verification packet: notarized share subscription agreement, corporate resolution, statement of compliance with the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia), register of directors and beneficial owners, source-of-funds documentation, and a letter from the remitter's bank confirming the remitter's identity. To avoid an unclean credit, remitters must remit from an account bearing the name of the subscribing entity or the disclosed beneficial owner.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for trade settlements and treasury transfers are executed through SWIFT MT103 customer transfers, SWIFT MT202 cover payments for bank-to-bank funds positioning, and, where letters of credit are used, commercial or standby letters of credit issued under UCP600 and curated by a licensed Canadian bank's trade finance department. Domestic CAD clearing is provided by Payments Canada's Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) or, for smaller payments, the retail Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS); United States dollar settlements clear through the Federal Reserve's Fedwire funds service or CHIPS. For family-office outward investment purchases, use institutional wire guidance with settlement instructions from the broker/custodian, including DTC settlement codes and ISIN references. Each disbursement must be supported by executed agreements, a treasury mandate, and, where the counterparty is a high-risk jurisdiction, additional legal opinions and beneficial ownership verification.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright foreign exchange forwards between CAD, USD, EUR, GBP, and other freely convertible currencies, typically with tenors under 24 months and supported by an ISDA 1998 FX definitions agreement.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies lacking onshore deliverable markets or where the counterparty bank's internal policy prohibits physical delivery, provided the net settlement currency is CAD or USD and the NDF is executed under a master FX agreement approved by legal counsel.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) and FX swaps to manage conversion risk on long-term family office assets, liabilities, and intercompany loans, executed on documented OTC terms with a Canadian Schedule I bank or a registered swap dealer and compliant with the board-approved treasury risk policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registrar of Companies (BC Registry, Ministry of Finance)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 months after the corporation's incorporation anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 85 (approx USD 62); continued default for 2 years triggers administrative strike-off; restoration possible by court order or registrar approval upon payment of arrears and penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A BC non-reporting private corporation is not statutorily required to undergo an independent audit unless: (i) it is a reporting issuer under securities law; (ii) shareholders holding at least 5% of the issued shares demand an audit; or (iii) specific regulations apply to the business (e.g., certain financial services). A single family office holding passive investments is generally audit-exempt, absent shareholder demand or regulatory requirement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for public/reporting issuers; ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) under Canadian GAAP for private companies unless shareholders elect otherwise.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate annual UBO filing is required in BC. The company must maintain a register of individuals with significant control (ISC) once it comes into existence, update it within 15 days of any change (e.g., share transfer), and keep it at the registered office or a prescribed BC location. The BC Annual Report requires confirmation of directors' particulars and address but does not include UBO data.
